clue.text: Support the environment through force of habit

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it
the natural world around us

explanation.surface: Someone backs green causes purely out of routine rather than conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Second nature is behaviour so ingrained by repetition that it feels instinctive, which is what habit's force produces.

clue.text: To wit, her weight rises with movement

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upwards, from the bottom

blocks.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for 'namely' or 'to wit'
taken as written
oz, ounce, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A woman's weight goes up as she exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: SC for scilicet is an old dictionary abbreviation the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively section of a symphony or sonata, and such a section is called a movement.

clue.text: Some hitch in the garlic supply?

blocks.note: first meaning: a ... hitch is a sailor's knot
second meaning: one segment of a garlic bulb

explanation.surface: A hold-up in the delivery of garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' reads as a snag, but it is the knot; 'Some' says this is one kind of hitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a common knot type, and a clove is the single bulb segment a cook takes from garlic.

clue.text: Such fluvial languages gathering nothing by ear

blocks.note: nil is zero
otic is the medical adjective meaning relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Languages of a river people picked up by listening rather than writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nilotic means of the Nile, and the Nilotic languages are spoken by peoples along it, hence 'fluvial'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic describes the language family of East African peoples living along the Nile river valley.

clue.text: See 1
John Brown's baby's cold remedy: take out a jar!

indicators.note: taking something out removes it, so the cold abbreviation is dropped from the remedy

blocks.note: in the song, John Brown's baby's cold was rubbed with camphorated oil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mock-urgent order to fetch a jar of the remedy from the old song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' does double duty: it describes the remedy and is also C, which comes out of CAMPHOR to leave AMPHOR, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage vessel for wine or oil.

clue.text: Sir Thomas Browne wrote to replace funeral tea supplier

indicators.note: read as re-place, it means put the two parts back in a different order from the one printed

blocks.note: an urn dispenses tea in quantity
a burial is a funeral rite

explanation.surface: The writer seems to have proposed swapping the tea urn at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts appear as funeral then tea supplier; re-placing them puts the urn first.
explanation.definitionFit: Urn Burial (Hydriotaphia, 1658) is Browne's famous meditation on ancient cremation urns found in Norfolk.

clue.text: As Milton was with no perception of his 22 in Gaza

definitions.text: with no perception of his 22 in Gaza

blocks.note: first meaning: the poet Milton was blind

blocks.clueFragment: with no perception of his 22 in Gaza
blocks.note: second meaning: Milton's phrase for his blinded Samson (22 across) in Samson Agonistes

explanation.surface: Blind Milton could not see the hero he wrote about.
explanation.walkthrough: Samson Agonistes has the blinded hero 'Eyeless in Gaza, at the mill with slaves', a phrase later used by Huxley as a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sight describes both the blind poet and his captive hero, whose eyes the Philistines put out.

clue.text: Make one of two

blocks.note: first meaning: join together into a single unit, as with railway wagons
second meaning: a pair

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as being one member of a pair; split it as 'Make one' and 'two'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to join or link things together, and the noun means a pair of anything.

clue.text: Juice extractors engendering motile hose panic

indicators.note: engendering means producing something new, so the following words are made into fresh arrangements

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Something squeezing juice makes a wriggling hose flap about.
explanation.walkthrough: Juice is slang for fuel, so the extractors are the firms that pump it out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil companies drill for and extract crude oil, the source of petrol, which is colloquially called juice.

clue.text: Critical Chaldean chap

blocks.note: Ur of the Chaldees, the Chaldean city in the Bible
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man from ancient Mesopotamia who is a sharp critic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something critical demands immediate attention, which is the sense of pressing or urgent.

clue.text: Old dog, before going out, runs to supplier of new tricks

indicators.note: the word for before goes on the outside, wrapping around the old dog

blocks.note: O abbreviates old
a cur is a mongrel dog
pre- means before
R is runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Plays on the saying that you can't teach an old dog new tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: A trick is slang for a prostitute's client, so the supplier is a pimp.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurer arranges sexual partners for others, providing a prostitute with fresh clients or 'tricks'.

clue.text: Hair grip needed here like a hole in the head

blocks.note: first meaning: the thing that holds a hair at its root
second meaning: a tiny pit in the scalp, taken literally

explanation.surface: Someone needs a hairgrip about as much as a hole in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom says something is not needed at all; here the hole in the head is literal and does the gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: A follicle is the small skin cavity from which each hair grows and where its root is held.

clue.text: Red falcon falling to an earthly host

indicators.note: something falling tumbles, so these letters land in a jumbled order

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A red bird of prey plummets towards someone receiving guests on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is an army, and a land force is an army operating on the ground rather than at sea or in the air.

clue.text: Surrounded with road hoardings: time to get out

indicators.note: hoarding means keeping something stored inside, so these boards hold the road

blocks.note: hoardings are billboards carrying advertisements
the M1, Britain's first motorway
T abbreviates time

explanation.surface: Hemmed in by roadside billboards, it's time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; hoardings both means advertisements and contains them. T gets out to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst is a preposition meaning in the middle of, as when one is enclosed by things on all sides.

clue.text: Beau-ideal having trouble with 'is new intake

indicators.note: an intake is something taken in, so the new letter goes inside

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
N abbreviates new
taken as written, a dropped-aitch his

explanation.surface: A handsome man struggling with his latest recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, names any strikingly handsome young man, the ideal of male beauty.

clue.text: Deciphering English codes, I see

indicators.note: deciphering untangles scrambled text, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: E abbreviates English
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A codebreaker announces that he understands English ciphers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' reads as 'I understand', but only 'see' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the area under a bishop's authority, which is exactly what a diocese is.

clue.text: Ruins the Porsche's lines, does it?

definitions.text: Ruins the Porsche's lines, does it?

blocks.clueFragment: Ruins the Porsche's lines, does it?
blocks.note: surface reading: something that wrecks a sports car's styling

blocks.clueFragment: Ruins the Porsche's lines, does it?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the rear aerofoil fitted to a sports car, whose name suggests that it spoils

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the pun: the part fitted to the back of a car is named as if it does damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear wing on a car disrupts airflow to add grip, and its name also means one who mars something.

clue.text: Man of the people puts oil distribution beyond pressure

indicators.note: distributing spreads things out in a new arrangement, so these letters are redealt

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
the fodder

explanation.surface: A politician with the common touch puts oil supply ahead of other pressures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond' places the rearranged letters after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A populist is a politician who claims to represent ordinary citizens against elites.

clue.text: French ready with chopper to cut such profits

blocks.note: pret is French for ready
ax, the American spelling of axe

explanation.surface: The French arrive ready with an axe to slash profits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the description of profits: pre-tax profits are what such profits are.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-tax profits are earnings counted before deductions for tax are made.

clue.text: Enthusiasm is rising between father and son

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upwards
between puts it inside, splitting the word for the son

blocks.note: pa is dad
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Excitement mounting in the household of a father and his boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion is intense, keen feeling, and enthusiasm is eager zeal for something.

clue.text: He suffered consonantly and so "madly set a thesis"

definitions.text: He suffered consonantly and so "madly set a thesis"

blocks.note: surface reading: a man afflicted in harmony, or in step
setter's reading: a man whose consonants swapped places, so a phrase came out muddled

explanation.walkthrough: The Rev William Spooner of Oxford reputedly swapped the first sounds of words, giving spoonerisms; 'consonantly' puns on consonants.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford don gave his name to the slip where initial sounds of two words trade places.

clue.text: Greek islander making hash of it in essence

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so these letters are jumbled
in places the jumbled letters inside the word for essence

blocks.note: the fodder
the core is the heart or essence

explanation.surface: A Greek islander cooks up a hash, perhaps of essences.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corfiote is a native or inhabitant of Corfu, one of the Ionian islands of Greece.

clue.text: Judge who contended with a bit of an ass

definitions.text: who contended with a bit of an ass

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the Judges, the leaders of Israel before its kings

blocks.clueFragment: who contended with a bit of an ass
blocks.note: second meaning: the strongman who fought the Philistines armed with a donkey's jawbone

explanation.surface: A magistrate who had to put up with a fool in court.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Judges he killed a thousand men with the jawbone of an ass, the 'bit of an ass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samson led Israel as one of the biblical Judges and is the hero famous for slaying Philistines with a jawbone.

clue.text: He did scream a lot round Norway!

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: much is a great amount
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A man who shrieked all the way round Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: Edvard Munch, a Norwegian, painted The Scream, so 'did scream' means painted it.
explanation.definitionFit: Munch is the Norwegian artist whose most famous painting is The Scream (1893).

clue.text: With this restriction, dissolute plier got on train

indicators.note: dissolute means loose and disorderly, so these letters are in disarray

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A debauched hawker boards a train despite some restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: A plier is one who plies a trade, such as a seller or a cab driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol rationing limits how much fuel each motorist may buy, as in wartime Britain or the 1970s crisis.

clue.text: Old, poor dear Plato's talking shop

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so these letters are put into a different form

blocks.note: ex- means former
the fodder

explanation.surface: An affectionate nod to the place where the old philosopher held forth.
explanation.definitionFit: An exedra was a recessed room or curved bench in Greek buildings where philosophers met for discussion.

clue.text: TV presenter staying in bed

blocks.note: first meaning: the lead presenter of a news programme
second meaning: the device that holds a ship by gripping the sea bed

explanation.surface: A newsreader who would rather stay under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is the sea bed, not a mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman fronts a broadcast, and a ship's anchor holds fast by lodging on the sea floor.
